# Data layer schema

*Generated by `python -m pipeline.run docs`. The prose is hand-written; every
column list, type and row count is introspected from the warehouse, so this
file cannot drift from the data.*

The warehouse has four layers. Each one is a directory or a file you can point
a tool at, and each is built by SQL you can read in `transforms/`.

```
video_data/*.mp4
      |
      |  pipeline/prepare.py          decode once -> cache/ (JPEG @ 4.0 Hz + 16 kHz WAV)
      v
 [1] warehouse/raw/<table>/<creative_id>.parquet
      |                               one file per extractor per creative
      |  transforms/01_raw_views.sql   views, so marts never touch file paths
      v
 [2] raw_* views in warehouse.duckdb
      |
      |  transforms/02..09             dimensions, spine, rollups
      v
 [3] tables in warehouse.duckdb       <- analysts query this
      |
      |  transforms/10_export_marts.sql
      v
 [4] warehouse/marts/*.parquet + .csv <- everything else reads this
```

## The nine extractors

| # | Extractor | Feature | Tool | Grain | Writes |
|---|-----------|---------|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | `metadata` v1.0 | Container, codec, resolution, frame-rate and audio-stream metadata | ffprobe (FFmpeg) | one row per creative; one row per sampled extractor | creative_metadata,sampling_config |
| 2 | `shots` v1.0 | Shot boundaries, shot count and shot durations (pacing) | PySceneDetect ContentDetector | one row per shot | shot_boundaries |
| 3 | `transcript` v1.0 | Spoken-word transcript with segment and word-level timestamps | faster-whisper 'small' (CTranslate2, int8 CPU) | one row per utterance; one row per word | transcript_segments,transcript_words,transcript_summary |
| 4 | `visual` v1.0 | Brightness, saturation, contrast, colourfulness, sharpness, edge density and frame-to-frame motion | OpenCV | one row per sampled frame (4.0 Hz) | visual_frames |
| 5 | `audio` v1.0 | Loudness (dBFS), tempo, spectral shape and harmonic/percussive balance | librosa | one row per sampled frame (4.0 Hz); one summary row per creative | audio_frames,audio_summary |
| 6 | `ocr` v1.0 | On-screen text detections (taglines, offers, captions, logotype) | RapidOCR (PP-OCRv4 ONNX) | one row per text detection per sampled frame (1.0 Hz) | screen_text_detections |
| 7 | `faces` v1.0 | Face count, face size/position on screen, and an 8-class facial expression per face | YuNet (detection) + FER+ (expression), both ONNX | one row per detected face per sampled frame (4.0 Hz) | face_detections |
| 8 | `objects` v1.0 | COCO-80 object and person detections with on-screen size and position | YOLOX-nano (ONNX) | one row per detection per sampled frame (2.0 Hz) | object_detections |
| 9 | `labels` v1.1 | Zero-shot semantic labels per shot across four axes (shot scale, setting, subject, style) | CLIP ViT-B/32 (int8 ONNX), zero-shot | one row per (shot, axis, label) | shot_label_scores |

Each extractor is one file in `pipeline/extractors/` exposing `NAME`,
`VERSION`, `FEATURE`, `TOOL`, `GRAIN`, `REQUIRES` and a single
`extract(prepared) -> dict[table_name, DataFrame]`. Adding a tenth signal is
one file plus one line in `pipeline/registry.py`.

## How to query it

```python
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect("warehouse/warehouse.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.sql("SELECT * FROM creative_summary").df()
```

or without this repo at all:

```python
import pandas as pd
pd.read_parquet("warehouse/marts/creative_seconds.parquet")
```

## Dimensions

### `creatives`

**Grain** one row per creative  ·  **Key** `creative_id`  ·  **Rows** 5

The creative dimension: file and codec facts plus whole-ad rollups of pacing, voice, sound and look.

> `creative_id` is a slug of the filename; `file_sha256` is the real version key. Re-encoding a video gives a new sha256 and re-triggers extraction.

> Use `display_name`, not `title`, for any chart, pivot or GROUP BY a human will read: titles are not unique (two sample creatives are the same campaign by different creators).

### `shots`

**Grain** one row per (creative, shot)  ·  **Key** `creative_id, shot_index`  ·  **Rows** 99

The unit a creative team thinks in. Carries CLIP's semantic labels plus what was visible and audible inside the shot.

> `label_*` is the winning label on that axis and `conf_*` its within-axis probability. A low `conf_*` means CLIP was genuinely unsure -- filter on it before trusting a label.

> `position_in_ad` lets you compare openings and end-frames across creatives of different lengths.

## Spine (time series)

### `creative_seconds`

**Grain** one row per (creative, second)  ·  **Key** `creative_id, second`  ·  **Rows** 391

THE JOIN TARGET for audience data. Everything that varies over time, aggregated to whole seconds.

> Biometric traces, dial tests and survey timestamps almost always arrive at 1 Hz. Join on (creative_id, second) -- no interpolation, no window functions.

> `audio_class` is the one field with judgement in it: speech is model-grounded (Whisper + Silero VAD), music vs ambient is a threshold stated in `transforms/07_creative_seconds.sql`.

> `max_objects` and `max_text_detections` are NULL for seconds whose frames were never sampled by that model -- see `sampling_config`.

### `creative_frames`

**Grain** one row per (creative, frame) at 4.0 Hz  ·  **Key** `creative_id, frame_index`  ·  **Rows** 1,557

The native grain. Use it when a sub-second event matters -- a 400 ms product reveal is invisible at 1 Hz.

> `frame_index` is 1-based; `t_start_s = (frame_index - 1) / 4.0`.

> NULL vs zero is meaningful. `n_objects` is NULL on frames YOLOX never looked at and 0 on frames it looked at and found nothing. The `objects_sampled` / `ocr_sampled` flags make that explicit.

> `is_cut` marks the first frame of every shot except the first, so `SUM(is_cut)` is a cut count.

|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |

## Language and text

### `transcript_segments`

**Grain** one row per spoken utterance  ·  **Key** `creative_id, segment_index`  ·  **Rows** 69

The script as Whisper heard it, with timings.

> `is_low_confidence` flags lines where Whisper's own `avg_logprob` or `no_speech_prob` suggests a hallucination -- common over instrumental music beds.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `segment_index` | BIGINT |
| `start_s` | DOUBLE |
| `end_s` | DOUBLE |
| `duration_s` | DOUBLE |
| `text` | VARCHAR |
| `n_words` | BIGINT |
| `words_per_s` | DOUBLE |
| `position_in_ad` | DOUBLE |
| `avg_logprob` | DOUBLE |
| `no_speech_prob` | DOUBLE |
| `compression_ratio` | DOUBLE |
| `is_low_confidence` | BOOLEAN |

### `transcript_words`

**Grain** one row per spoken word  ·  **Key** `creative_id, segment_index, word_index`  ·  **Rows** 726

Word-level timings, for locating a brand mention to the half-second.

> `word_norm` is lowercased and stripped of punctuation, so joining a brand-term list needs no cleaning.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `segment_index` | BIGINT |
| `word_index` | BIGINT |
| `word` | VARCHAR |
| `word_norm` | VARCHAR |
| `start_s` | DOUBLE |
| `end_s` | DOUBLE |
| `probability` | DOUBLE |
| `position_in_ad` | DOUBLE |

### `screen_text`

**Grain** one row per on-screen text span  ·  **Key** `creative_id, screen_text_id`  ·  **Rows** 480

On-screen copy as time spans: a tagline held for four seconds is one row, not four detections.

> `is_large_text` and `vertical_position` approximate the role of the copy -- headline versus legal line -- without anyone watching the ad.

> OCR is imperfect on stylised type. `max_score` is the recogniser's confidence; filter on it for clean text.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `screen_text_id` | BIGINT |
| `text` | VARCHAR |
| `text_norm` | VARCHAR |
| `start_s` | DOUBLE |
| `end_s` | DOUBLE |
| `duration_s` | DOUBLE |
| `n_frames_present` | BIGINT |
| `max_score` | DOUBLE |
| `max_height_frac` | DOUBLE |
| `mean_centre_y` | DOUBLE |
| `is_large_text` | BOOLEAN |
| `vertical_position` | VARCHAR |

## Detections

### `face_detections`

**Grain** one row per detected face per sampled frame  ·  **Key** `creative_id, frame_index, face_index`  ·  **Rows** 1,789

Every face on screen, with its size, position and an 8-class expression.

> `p_*` columns are the full expression distribution, not just the winner. They are NULL when the face was too small to classify (recorded as present but unlabelled rather than guessed at).

> This measures the expressions of actors *in the ad*, which is not the same construct as a viewer's expression. See the README note on where viewer-side measurement plugs in.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `frame_index` | BIGINT |
| `t_start_s` | DOUBLE |
| `face_index` | BIGINT |
| `score` | DOUBLE |
| `x0` | DOUBLE |
| `y0` | DOUBLE |
| `x1` | DOUBLE |
| `y1` | DOUBLE |
| `area_frac` | DOUBLE |
| `centre_x` | DOUBLE |
| `centre_y` | DOUBLE |
| `is_largest` | BOOLEAN |
| `emotion_top` | VARCHAR |
| `emotion_top_prob` | DOUBLE |
| `p_neutral` | DOUBLE |
| `p_happiness` | DOUBLE |
| `p_surprise` | DOUBLE |
| `p_sadness` | DOUBLE |
| `p_anger` | DOUBLE |
| `p_disgust` | DOUBLE |
| `p_fear` | DOUBLE |
| `p_contempt` | DOUBLE |
| `position_in_ad` | DOUBLE |

### `object_detections`

**Grain** one row per detection per sampled frame  ·  **Key** `creative_id, frame_index, detection_index`  ·  **Rows** 2,381

COCO-80 objects and people, with on-screen size and position.

> COCO has no class for 'lip oil' or 'football shirt'. Treat this as coarse scene composition (how many people, is there a car, a phone, a bottle), not product recognition.

> `area_frac` is the share of the frame the box covers, so 'product fills the screen' is a filter, not an eyeball judgement.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `frame_index` | BIGINT |
| `t_start_s` | DOUBLE |
| `detection_index` | BIGINT |
| `class_id` | BIGINT |
| `class_name` | VARCHAR |
| `score` | DOUBLE |
| `x0` | DOUBLE |
| `y0` | DOUBLE |
| `x1` | DOUBLE |
| `y1` | DOUBLE |
| `area_frac` | DOUBLE |
| `position_in_ad` | DOUBLE |

### `shot_label_scores`

**Grain** one row per (creative, shot, axis, label)  ·  **Key** `creative_id, shot_index, axis, label`  ·  **Rows** 1,683

Every CLIP label with its score, not just the winner.

> Scores are softmaxed *within* an axis, so they sum to 1 per (shot, axis) and are comparable only inside an axis.

> `shots` holds the pivoted winners; use this table when the runner-up or the margin matters.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `shot_index` | BIGINT |
| `axis` | VARCHAR |
| `label` | VARCHAR |
| `score` | DOUBLE |
| `rank` | BIGINT |
| `is_top` | BOOLEAN |
| `n_frames_scored` | BIGINT |

## Provenance

### `run_manifest`

**Grain** one row per (creative, extractor) run  ·  **Key** `creative_id, extractor`  ·  **Rows** 50

Provenance. Which extractor version produced which rows, when, how long it took, and whether it failed.

> A failed extractor does not abort the run, so this is where you check that the data you are about to analyse actually exists.

> `creative_sha256` ties rows to exact video bytes.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `creative_sha256` | VARCHAR |
| `extractor` | VARCHAR |
| `extractor_version` | VARCHAR |
| `status` | VARCHAR |
| `rows_written` | BIGINT |
| `tables` | VARCHAR |
| `run_id` | VARCHAR |
| `finished_at` | VARCHAR |
| `duration_s` | DOUBLE |
| `error` | INTEGER |

### `sampling_config`

**Grain** one row per (creative, subsampled extractor)  ·  **Key** `creative_id, extractor`  ·  **Rows** 25

The sampling rate each model actually ran at, so the warehouse describes its own resolution.

> `step_frames = frame_hz / sample_hz`. Used by the SQL to tell 'never sampled' apart from 'sampled, found nothing'.

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| `creative_id` | VARCHAR |
| `extractor` | VARCHAR |
| `sample_hz` | DOUBLE |
| `frame_hz` | DOUBLE |
| `step_frames` | BIGINT |
